newsitem.title: CHILE: Cochilco raises 1997 copper price forecast.
newsitem.headline: Cochilco raises 1997 copper price forecast.

text.p: Chile's state copper studies board Cochilco said it raised its forecast of average copper prices this year to $1-$1.05 per lb from earlier estimates of $1 despite a sharp increase in Chilean copper output.
"A supply deficit is projected for this year and so prices should be reasonable," said Sergio Garcia, head of research at the Comision Chilena del Cobre (Cochilco).
Chile's Central Bank increased this week its own forecast of copper prices to $1 a pound from $0.95 assumed in the country's budget presented to Congress in September.
The Bank traditionally takes a more conservative view than Cochilco of the outlook for copper prices.
Rising demand will soak up the steep increase in output expected in coming years from Chile, the world's largest copper producer, and so copper prices should remain stable, he said.
"There is a very good rythym of growth in demand... and no risk of production stagnating," said Garcia.
"There are no elements which make us think that income from copper will fall."
Copper is Chile's largest export and accounts for around a third of export income.
Figures from Cochilco show copper output soaring to 4.86 tonnes by the end of the decade from 3.1 million tonnes last year as new mines are brought into operation and existing pits expand.
Output is seen rising this year to 3.4 million tonnes.
